propositions: A single pending entry disables the O(1) fast path marker for the entire store, causing every subsequent write to perform a full O(store-size) walk of ticket directories
The marker is only written when a full scan finds no pending entries, resulting in binary all-or-nothing behavior rather than proportional cost scaling
On a 4,938-ticket store with one pending entry, write latency is ~1.2-1.3 seconds compared to ~0.11 ms when the marker engages (4,800x slower)
Redesign the gate marker to record a 'live' set of ticket ids with enqueued non-DONE entries, allowing scoped walks of O(backlog) instead of O(store) when the marker cannot prove store-wide quiet
Scoped marker probes must never refresh the TTL (written_ns), preserving the bound measured from the last full walk and maintaining the append-during-scan race invariant
